research_question: Hvordan avgrenses perioder, stiler og epoker, og hvilke anakronismer oppstår når senere kategorier legges bakover i tid?

bibliographic_identity.title: Dönemlendirme Çalışmaları ve Osmanlı-Türk Müziği Tarihyazımı: Bir Bilanço Denemesi

production_source_extensions.registration_reason: Open-access research article that compares multiple Ottoman-Turkish music periodization schemes, documents institutional uptake of Berker's model, contrasts composer/label and analytical-source approaches, and shows how expansion of the Kevserî source corpus changes the confidence that can be placed in period boundaries.

Original full-text periodization proposal used as one concrete chronology for comparison. It divides the history into preparatory, classical, neoclassical, romantic and reform phases using named composer boundaries and period labels.

bibliographic_identity.title: Türk Müziği Tarihinde Yeni Bir Dönemlendirme Önerisi

production_source_extensions.registration_reason: Alternative full-text periodization proposal that reorganizes Turkish music history around changing source regimes and historiographic criteria: archaeological, paleographic, systematist, classical Turkish music and popularization periods.

locators.supports: Fırat reproduces Berker's composer-bounded preparatory/classical/neoclassical/romantic/reform scheme and notes that it became widespread in applied contexts and was used in the Istanbul Technical University Turkish Music State Conservatory curriculum before being replaced in 2000 by a century-based curriculum.

Fırat summarizes Feldman's eight-period 1500–1850 peşrev chronology based on form, makam, seyir, melodic density and named source/repertoire clusters, demonstrating a periodization logic different from Berker's imported-style labels and composer boundaries.

Fırat explains that some eighteenth-century claims by Feldman and Wright rested on a few published Kevserî peşrevs; later work on a much broader notation corpus required those conclusions to be revisited, and Fırat makes source diversity a central criterion for defensible periodization.

locators.supports: Uslu proposes a paleographic period beginning with the Orkhon inscriptions and an earlier archaeological period for music history reconstructed from non-written archaeological and cultural evidence, explicitly changing the source regime used to define the period.

Uslu proposes the sequence Archaeological, Paleographic, Systematists, Classical Turkish Music and Popularization, and places the post-classical popularization phase from the mid-nineteenth century while discussing multiple cultural groups and source traditions.

claim_records.statement: I det avgrensede korpuset for osmansk-tyrkisk musikkhistoriografi gir ulike periodiseringsvalg forskjellige historiske kart: Berkers mye brukte modell organiserer historien gjennom komponistgrenser og etiketter som klassisk, neoklassisk, romantisk og reform, mens Uslu organiserer en alternativ kronologi rundt skiftende kilderegimer og historiografiske kriterier som arkeologisk, paleografisk, systematikere, klassisk tyrkisk musikk og popularisering. Fırats sammenligning viser i tillegg at stil- og repertoaranalytiske modeller endrer overgangspunktene, og at utvidelse av Kevserî-korpuset krevde revisjon av enkelte 1700-tallsslutninger. Periodisering kan derfor behandles som en kildeavhengig analytisk modell som gjør ulike aktører, praksiser og kildetyper synlige, ikke som en nøytral kalender eller én universelt riktig kronologi.
locators: Fırat 2019 pp. 155–156: Berker model, institutional uptake and curriculum replacement
Fırat 2019 pp. 156–158: Feldman analytical chronology and Kevserî source-base revision

object_scope.source_test: Kevserî notation-corpus expansion as a documented challenge to conclusions drawn from a small published subset
object_scope.evidence_role: comparison of historiographic period models and source dependence, not adjudication of a single true chronology

claim_records.uncertainty: The corpus compares a small number of published periodization proposals and Fırat's review of related analytical work. It does not exhaust Ottoman-Turkish music historiography, and the models differ in scope: some address broad Turkish music history while others focus more narrowly on Ottoman court/instrumental repertoire. Uslu's categories and Berker's labels remain historiographic proposals rather than independently measured natural periods.
claim_records.prohibited_inference: Do not infer that one model is universally correct, that period boundaries are objective facts, that all Turkish/Ottoman regions and communities follow the same chronology, that imported European period labels are automatically invalid, or that the Kevserî source expansion nullifies every long-duration style observation.

resolved: Fırat 2019 has persistent journal identity, DOI, page range and open-access full text.
The direct object contains explicit locators for Berker's periodization, Feldman's alternative analytical chronology and the Kevserî source-corpus revision problem.
Berker 1985 and Uslu 2015 are independently reviewed full-text periodization proposals with different organizing criteria.
At least two competing periodizations are therefore inspectable, and the source-corpus counterexample makes the evidential dependence of boundaries explicit.
Inference boundaries block universal chronology, scope overreach, institutional-validity substitution and total-refutation claims.
The article object is delivered as external_link_and_metadata_only.
direct_object_gate.release_rule: Only the bounded claim that periodization models organize this corpus differently and depend on source selection may drive questions. Preserve differences of scope and do not promote any scheme to a universal chronology.

coverage.known_gap: This production does not exhaust Ottoman-Turkish music historiography or compare every region, oral tradition, genre or community. It verifies one bounded comparison of published periodization models and one documented source-corpus revision problem.
